title: Festivals in their cultural context
subtitle: festivities, celebratory, commemorate, flamboyant, pagan
summary: Describe festivals in formal English - what they celebrate, commemorate and symbolise, what they feature, and whether the atmosphere is festive, flamboyant, raucous or sombre.

lesson.heading: Describing a festival
lesson.text: The Mombasa Carnival **falls** in November each year - a festival **falls** on a date. People travel there to **participate in the festivities**, the enjoyable activities. The carnival **features** people in spectacular costumes **parading** through the streets. Promoting integration remains the **focus** of the carnival.

examples.text: The festival always **falls** on the first Monday in July.
The **festivities** included parades, sports and musical gatherings.
Spring flowers were the main **focus** of the festival.
On the anniversary of the battle, soldiers **paraded** through the streets.

lesson.heading: Noun, verb and adjective
lesson.note: There is no verb for spectacle and no adjective for parade.

lesson.heading: Using the word family
lesson.text: A **feast** is a big meal to celebrate something; during a national holiday there may be a whole week of **feasting**. A festival can be a time of **renewal** - each year it **renews** the national spirit of the people. Many **customs** have their origin in ancient **ceremonies**.

examples.text: For Christians, Christmas **celebrates** the birth of Jesus Christ.
There was a **celebratory** feeling about the whole weekend.
People were in a **festive** mood when a huge **feast** was held in the village.
The spring festival is a **renewal** of the fertility of the land.

lesson.heading: Spectacles and processions
lesson.text: A **spectacle** is an impressive public display, and something impressive is **spectacular**. A **ceremonial** procession is one performed with formal ritual.

examples.text: You should go and see the lantern festival. It's always a **spectacle**.
The gymnastic display involving 300 children was really **spectacular**.
There was a **ceremonial** atmosphere as the military bands **paraded** around the main square.

lesson.heading: Anniversaries and remembering
lesson.text: A **centenary** is a 100th anniversary and a **bi-centenary** a 200th. To **commemorate** something is to respect and remember it officially; this is a formal word.

examples.text: It was the **centenary** of the founding of the university and the **bi-centenary** of the city itself.
The annual holiday **commemorates** all those who died in the country's civil war.
The festival always falls on the first Monday in July. It **commemorates** a famous battle.

lesson.heading: The atmosphere of a festival
rows: having a special feeling or atmosphere
having illogical beliefs about hidden forces in nature
from the times when people believed nature had special powers

lesson.heading: Origins and meanings
lesson.text: A tradition can be **traced back to** an earlier period - its origin may be found there. Things **symbolise** ideas, and festivals are **associated with** seasons or events.

examples.text: The Festival of the Dead is very **sombre** and **atmospheric**.
It can be **traced back to pagan** times.
The festival was **associated with** the coming of spring, after the **sombre** winter months.

lesson.text: A festival falls on a date and is held in a place - and it commemorates a person or event, but celebrates a happy occasion.

exercises.prompt: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.right: from the times when nature was believed to have special powers
having illogical beliefs about hidden forces

exercises.prompt: The festival events included parades, sports and musical gatherings. The ___ included parades, sports and musical gatherings.
exercises.explanation: Festivities are the enjoyable activities that make up a festival.

exercises.prompt: There was a ___ feeling about the whole weekend.
exercises.explanation: Celebratory is the adjective from celebration: everyone was in a celebratory mood.

exercises.prompt: People were in a ___ mood when the harvest was successfully completed.
exercises.explanation: There was a festive mood in the village during the spring holiday.

exercises.prompt: For people who live in the country, the spring festival is a ___ of the fertility of the land.
exercises.explanation: A festival can be a time of renewal - it renews the spirit of the people.

exercises.prompt: There was a ___ atmosphere as the military bands paraded around the main square.
exercises.explanation: A ceremonial procession goes through the streets of the city.

exercises.prompt: It was the ___ of the founding of the university, exactly one hundred years before.
exercises.explanation: A centenary is a 100th anniversary; a bi-centenary is a 200th.

exercises.prompt: Its origin can be ___ back to the religious tradition of taking flowers to the gods.
exercises.explanation: If something can be traced back to a period, its origin may be found there.

exercises.prompt: The festival is always on the first Monday in July. It is in memory of a famous battle. Which verbs are correct?
options: It falls on the first Monday in July and commemorates a famous battle.
It parades on the first Monday in July and celebrates a famous battle.
It features the first Monday in July and renews a famous battle.
It is held the first Monday in July and symbolises a famous battle.
exercises.explanation: A festival falls on a date, and commemorates - respects and remembers officially - an event.

exercises.prompt: The gymnastic display involving 300 children was a real spectacle. Rewritten with an adjective, this is:
exercises.explanation: There is no verb for spectacle; the adjective is spectacular.

exercises.prompt: The Rio de Janeiro Carnival is always a very ___ and ___ event: extremely colourful and very noisy.
exercises.explanation: Flamboyant means extremely colourful and exaggerated; raucous means very noisy.

exercises.statement: Nowadays most people are not so superstitious, but there are still some pagan festivals celebrated every year.
exercises.explanation: Correct - superstitious means having illogical beliefs about hidden forces in nature, and pagan festivals come from the times when nature was thought to have special powers.

exercises.statement: The Festival of the Dead is very flamboyant and raucous: it is serious, heavy and sad.
exercises.explanation: The Festival of the Dead is very sombre and atmospheric. Flamboyant and raucous mean colourful and noisy.

exercises.prompt: Is each word a noun, a verb or an adjective in this word family?
Put this sentence about a spring festival in order.
exercises.answer: The flowers symbolised new life and the festival was very atmospheric
exercises.explanation: To symbolise is to represent an idea; atmospheric means having a special feeling.
